ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, triangle $\triangle ABC$ is folded along line $l$, positioning point $B$ on point $F$. If $\angle 1 - \angle 2 = 70^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, \\
due to the property of folding, we have: $\angle F=\angle B$, \\
according to the external angle property of triangles, we get: $\angle 1=\angle 3+\angle B$, $\angle 2=\angle 3-\angle F=\angle 3-\angle B$, \\
$\therefore \angle 1-\angle 2=\angle 3+\angle B-(\angle 3-\angle B)=2\angle B=70^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle B=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

Therefore, $\angle 1-\angle 2=\angle 3+\angle B-(\angle 3-\angle B)=2\angle B=70^\circ$, so $\angle B=35^\circ$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, triangle $\triangle ABC$ is folded along line $l$, positioning point $B$ on point $F$. If $\angle 1 - \angle 2 = 70^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle B$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Due to the property of folding, we have $\angle F=\angle B$. According to the exterior angle property of triangles, $\angle 1=\angle 3+\angle B$ and $\angle 2=\angle 3-\angle F=\angle 3-\angle B$. Therefore, $\angle 1-\angle 2=\angle 3+\angle B-(\angle 3-\angle B)=2\angle B=70^\circ$, so $\angle B=35^\circ$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is triangle ABC, point A is at the upper left, point C is at the lower left, and point B is on the right side; the broken line l passes near the interior of the triangle, point D is in the upper part, and point E is near the lower right part. Dashed lines point from D and E to B on the right side, indicating the line segments related to B before folding; after folding, point B falls to point F, and point F is at the lower left of E. Angles 1 and 2 are marked in the figure, and auxiliary angle ∠3 can be introduced to represent the common angle in angle tracking near D/E.
Reasoning: Folding is a reflection transformation and preserves the size of angles, so the corresponding angle at point F after folding is equal to the original ∠B, that is, ∠F = ∠B. From the exterior angle relationship in the figure, we can obtain ∠1 = ∠3 + ∠B; at the same time ∠2 = ∠3 - ∠F. Substituting ∠F = ∠B, we get ∠2 = ∠3 - ∠B. Therefore ∠1 - ∠2 = (∠3 + ∠B) - (∠3 - ∠B) = 2∠B. It is known that ∠1 - ∠2 = 70°, so 2∠B = 70°, and solving gives ∠B = 35°.
